en.title: Nintendo Gears Up for Two Massive Directs: Zelda 40th and More!
en.summary: Get ready, gamers! Nintendo is set to unleash two major Nintendo Direct presentations back-to-back, focusing on the monumental 40th anniversary of The Legend of Zelda and a broader look at upcoming titles.
en.body:
The gaming world is abuzz with anticipation as Nintendo prepares to host not one, but two highly anticipated Nintendo Direct presentations this September. The first, scheduled for Tuesday, September 8, will be a special celebration of The Legend of Zelda's 40th anniversary, followed by a general Nintendo Direct on Wednesday, September 9. These events are poised to deliver significant news for fans across the globe, with particular excitement surrounding the iconic Zelda franchise.

## Zelda's Diamond Anniversary Direct

The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct is expected to be the crown jewel of this two-day event. While details remain speculative, the centerpiece is almost certainly the full reveal of the **The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time** remake. After a tantalizingly brief teaser earlier this year, fans are eager for a comprehensive look at this beloved classic's reimagining for modern hardware. Questions about its faithfulness to the original, the scope of its graphical overhaul, and a definitive release date are at the forefront of many minds. Beyond Ocarina of Time, whispers suggest potential announcements related to the franchise's future, possibly including a new entry or significant content for the rumored **Switch 2** console, which has been hinted at in leaked imagery tied to the anniversary.

## What Else to Expect

The general Nintendo Direct following the Zelda celebration is also packed with potential. While the specifics are scarce, the industry is rife with predictions. Fans are hoping for updates on **Fire Emblem: Fortune's Weave**, a title that has generated considerable buzz. Furthermore, a **Metroid Prime Trilogy HD Pack** has been a long-standing request, and its shadow drop announcement wouldn't be out of the question given Nintendo's penchant for surprises. The possibility of ports for major titles like **Baldur's Gate 3** on the Switch 2 also remains a hot topic. The Mario 40th anniversary was notably featured in a past September Direct, suggesting that Nintendo often uses these showcases for significant franchise milestones, making the Zelda event a prime candidate for major reveals.

## Fan Frenzy and Future Gazing

These upcoming Directs represent more than just game announcements; they are pivotal moments for the passionate Nintendo community. The potential reveal of an **Ocarina of Time** remake, a title many consider a masterpiece, carries immense weight. News regarding the **Switch 2**’s launch titles, especially if tied to the Zelda anniversary, could shape the next generation of Nintendo gaming. The community is abuzz with speculation, dissecting every rumor and leak, eager to see which predictions will materialize. The blend of nostalgia for Zelda's past and anticipation for Nintendo's future ensures these Directs will be closely watched.

## What's Next

Mark your calendars for September 8th and 9th. While official times are yet to be confirmed, these dates are the focal point for what promises to be an unforgettable showcase of Nintendo's upcoming slate.

content_raw: Nintendo is hosting two Directs in the coming days , and it’s pretty much all I’ve been thinking about since the announcement. On Tuesday, September 8, it’s The Legend of Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct, followed by a more general Nintendo Direct on Wednesday, September 9. While we wait, it's predictions time! Before we start, a couple of disclaimers: these are all purely my guesses based on public information and my analysis of Nintendo’s release patterns, and nothing more. Nothing here is based on any inside information. But, I will be discussing a couple of relevant leaks over the last few months, so if you have been steering clear of information like that, you may not want to read on. Zelda 40th Anniversary Direct Predictions Zelda is my favorite series, so I’m buzzing thinking about all the possibilities we could see Tuesday morning. But I’m trying to keep things realistic in this piece and only sharing predictions that I think have a legitimate chance of happening. The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time’s Full Reveal This will undoubtedly be the centerpiece of the presentation. We’ve only seen a few seconds of footage of the Ocarina of Time remake , which is set to come out in 2026. So, now’s the time for the full reveal trailer and release date. I can’t wait for this one; my imagination has been running wild over this remake for the last three months, and we’re finally going to see more about the scope of this remake. Is it faithful, or more of a reimagining? What does the kingdom of Hyrule look like beyond Link’s treehouse? All that and more will likely be answered by a more conventional trailer that gives us a proper look at the remake. I don’t know exactly what Ocarina of Time will look like, but the teaser trailer from earlier this year tells me Nintendo is very confident in this game. You don’t set the internet’s imagination on fire with a 10-second tease of Link’s treehouse if you don’t have really satisfying answers to share when you do finally pull the curtain back, and I expect the Ocarina of Time remake to be a pretty big deal. Ocarina of Time's Release Date As for a release date, I’m expecting Ocarina of Time to arrive on Thursday, November 12. Nintendo doesn’t have a game dated for November yet (Fire Emblem arrives this month, with Nintendo Switch Sports slated for October), and it never misses putting out a big game in the weeks before Black Friday. Knowing it’s coming this year, Zelda feels primed for that spot. Nintendo is extremely unlikely to release a game on Thanksgiving (that’s Thursday, November 26 in the U.S.), and it has no reason to go head-to-head with Grand Theft Auto VI on November 19. That just leaves November 5 and 12 as available Thursdays to launch a game. A few weeks back, the Nintendo UK store briefly dated a couple of Kirby Air Riders amiibo for November 12 , and Nintendo typically launches amiibo the same day as a first-party game, even if the franchises aren’t related.
